verdict.rationale: YYLO's `task start` creates a dedicated branch/worktree from a frozen target SHA and runs configured dependency hydration before work begins, so the product itself sets up an isolated working copy with dependencies installed. However, this is a worktree of an existing checkout rather than a documented repo clone, and hydration is whatever the operator configures, not the agent setting up its own environment. Missing for 10: documented cloning of a remote repo, agent-driven (not pre-configured) dependency install and environment configuration, details of what hydration supports, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent automatically clone the repo, install dependencies, and configure its own working environment

citations.quote: `task start` freezes the protected target SHA, creates a dedicated branch/worktree, and completes configured dependency hydration before reporting `WORKING`.
Start hydrates an exact-base task worktree.
Execute candidates in private fresh repositories, not shared task worktrees.
